scientificChecks.boundedAtomAndScope: One introductory explanatory consumer-choice competence, retaining needs/preferences, budget and information. Supplied model explanation does not establish autonomous model construction or whole primary-source coverage.
scientificChecks.ordinarySufficientWork: Explains both supplied households: affordability, ordinal ranking, A-to-D demand changes, controlled attention, legitimate different preferences; transfers to total costs, use needs and missing durability information.
counterPerformances: Computes all prices correctly but labels fully informed Mila irrational solely because Lea ranks A first, or treats ordinal ranks as objective/interpersonally comparable total utility.
Observes B without matched information and infers certain inattention; alternatively ignores the explicit finite menu and uses an unoffered combination as the model solution.
Chooses an environmental-sounding product without linking needs, initial affordability, total cost and available information; preference rhetoric alone does not establish the interaction.

firstFictionalHousehold.context: Weekly bicycle rentals b and bus rides t; all essentials separately funded. Supplier offers only A=(2,2), B=(0,3), C=(2,1), D=(0,1). Budget EUR 9, b EUR 1, t EUR 3, explicit full preference order A>C>B>D includes remaining money.
firstFictionalHousehold.controlledInformation: At original prices only B,D are considered, so B is selected; compare all A-D visible with needs/prices/ranking unchanged. Another fully informed household can legitimately rank B first.

secondFictionalHousehold.context: Six-month use of an appliance; closed exclusive alternatives A refurbished ownership EUR 70 upfront plus EUR 2/month running cost, B rental with no deposit EUR 15/month, C new ownership EUR 55 upfront plus EUR 6/month. All other spending funded. Full fixed order A>B>C includes end-of-horizon value and remaining money; initial budget EUR 60, total six-month budget EUR 95, monthly rental allowance EUR 15. No credit or other offers.
secondFictionalHousehold.initialDemand: B: six rental months, no purchased appliance
secondFictionalHousehold.changedFunding: EUR 20 grant raises initial budget to EUR 80 and total to EUR 115; all relevant preferences, costs and offers unchanged.
secondFictionalHousehold.changedDemand: A: one refurbished appliance, no rental months
secondFictionalHousehold.attentionAndLimits: After the grant, consideration restricted to B,C still selects B; matched full-menu comparison can examine this stipulated attention mechanism. Different needs/environment weights may yield another legitimate order; if durability or running costs cease to be known, the six-month comparison must be qualified and missing information identified.

alternativeSufficientDemonstration.adequacy: Together these give two independently explained household demands, a real price and a financing variation, a controlled consideration mechanism, forgone alternatives and meaningful intertemporal/initial-versus-total-budget transfer. They are hypothetical reviewer counterchecks, not observed learner performance or new P cases; labels or extra-task quotas are not evidence.

scientificChecks.orientationBoundary: Existing fachfree orientation requires/tests no knowledge and adds no macroeconomic competence. Its separate non-graded completion policy remains applicable; selection of an interest label does not itself certify completion.
scientificChecks.imageBoundary: Original PNG and current native page both show comparison of two backpacks with budget, practical use and social thoughts. Fits teaching support; no image acceptance or learner evidence is inferred.
